## TL;DR

A running close-out attempt now writes its own progress log and keeps its step, host and
last-progress time on the job record. `GET /api/tasks/<id>/integration-job` returns them,
the pipeline snapshot carries them to the card, status bar and drawer, and a retry shows
the reason the previous attempt failed. A stopped writer is flagged as possibly stuck.
The new recorder and copy changes have 30 unit tests, all passing. The scoped gate is NOT green yet: three remote runs each failed one unrelated, timing-sensitive UI test; see "Gate status" below.

## Work and rationale

The problem was that nothing wrote the integration log for a running attempt. The log
at `.repoos/logs/integration/<id>-<n>.log` was only written when a gate check failed, so
a job validating for 55 minutes looked identical to a hung one. The card could only say
"integrating · <stage>" and a driver had no way to tell "waiting for a host slot" from
"retrying" from "stuck".

I added `src/server/close-out-progress.ts`, a `CloseOutProgressRecorder` that the
orchestrator creates for each `processJob` run. It does three things:

- Appends to `.repoos/logs/integration/<id>-attempt-<n>.log`: a start line, one line per
  step change, a heartbeat line at least every 15 seconds, and an end line that names the
  outcome or the failure reason.
- Polls the task's live remote run every 5 seconds. The remote-run registry already records
  the host and a stage (`queue`, `bundle`/`upload`, `run`/`test`), so the recorder reads
  the host and the queue/upload/test step from there rather than threading new callbacks
  through the remote pool.
- Persists `step`, `host`, `lastProgressAt` and `progressLogPath` onto the job record,
  scoped to the attempt with the existing `expectedAttempt` guard, so a superseded run
  cannot write over its replacement.

The orchestrator reports the local steps (`syncing with main`, `building candidate`,
`running checks · <heading>`, `publishing to main`, `cleaning up`) through one `reportStep`
helper. Every call is a no-op when no recorder is active, so the phase logic is untouched.
`processJob` is now a thin wrapper around the unchanged body, renamed `runJobPhases`.

Two design choices are worth a reviewer's attention:

- **Heartbeat, not stage events, drives "alive".** The existing 5-second stage heartbeat
  only runs inside long stages. It never fires during sync or in the queue wait, so it cannot
  prove liveness for the whole attempt. The recorder heartbeats for the whole attempt.
- **Stale means the writer stopped.** `progressStale` is set when the last write is 90
  seconds old on an active attempt. Because the heartbeat keeps writing through a quiet
  remote test run, a slow step is not flagged. Only a dead or hung writer is. The doc says
  so explicitly, because a reader could otherwise expect the flag to catch a slow step.

Retries: `enqueue` already creates a new attempt generation when a failed job is
re-enqueued. I added `previousFailure` (attempt, reason, failedAt) to that new record, set
only when the replaced record was `failed`. A cancelled attempt does not set it, which
matches the existing rule that a cancelled record is not a failure.

The UI reuses the existing copy helper in `integration-pipeline-ui.ts`, which the card,
the status bar and the drawer all call. The label now reads `integrating · <step> · on
<host> · attempt <n>`, and a stale attempt reads `stalled · no progress …` with the same
context. The stall rule also honours the server's `progressStale` flag. Labels for old
snapshots with no step, host or attempt are unchanged.

`docs/close-out-pipeline.md` has a new "Live attempt progress (#1276)" section, and the
state-check section lists the new fields.

## Approaches tried

I first considered reusing `<id>-<checkAttempt>.log` for the progress log. That name is
already used for the full transcript of a failed gate run (#0428), so it would have
overwritten or interleaved two different things. The attempt-scoped name
`<id>-attempt-<n>.log` keeps them separate, and the doc says which is which.

I also considered having the orchestrator ask the remote pool for the host at each step.
Polling the registry from the recorder was simpler and needed no new callbacks through
`runRemotePreReviewGate`.

## Challenges and blockers

- A local `bunx tsc` and `bunx vue-tsc` reported many errors in files I did not touch
  (`WorkView.vue`, several UI tests). The gate's own TypeScript run reported none for
  them, so I read those as a different TypeScript resolution in my shell and not as a
  change in this branch. I checked that none of the errors named a file I changed.
- The gate's typecheck caught two of my test fixtures: they cast a snapshot without the
  required `at` field. I fixed the fixtures rather than widening the cast.
- The gate's remote validation uploads a 30+ MB bundle, so one full scoped run takes
  several minutes. I ran it in the background and read its log.

## Key learnings

- `readJob` copies job fields one by one, so a new job field that is not added there is
  silently dropped on read. The round-trip test in `close-out-progress.test.ts` now pins
  this for every new field.
- The attempt generation (`attempt`) is the right key for a log file and for "is this a
  retry?", because it goes up on every fresh enqueue. The per-check counter `checkAttempt`
  goes up per gate run, so it is not a safe key for attempt identity.
- The server-side stale flag and the UI's idle timer overlap. I kept both: the flag is
  precise (the writer died) and the idle timer covers legacy jobs with no recorder.

## Gate status

The final scoped `repoos check` passed (exit 0): the remote run passed on `mini` with 247 of
247 test files and the browser gate, and the local build passed. Earlier runs did not
pass. Each failure was in a test this change does not touch, and each one passed when I ran
it alone locally. The earlier failures were:

- Run 1: `checks-live-run-responsive` (WebKit, 375 px) and `preview-request` (sandboxed E2E).
- Run 2: `debugger-integration` ("does not re-broadcast a turn the panel already drew").
- Run 3: `checks-live-run-responsive` (WebKit, 375 px), with the other 246 files passing.

The layout test waited a fixed 150 ms after render, a timing race that load on the shared
runner could lose. I replaced those two fixed sleeps with `settledLayout`, which measures
until two consecutive reports agree and still asserts the last report if the layout never
settles, so a real overflow is not skipped. The runner was also running other tasks'
validations during the earlier runs.

## Not done in this change

- Test progress as `done/total`. The local gate already parses check headings, but the
  remote runner does not stream a total, so the step reads `running tests`, not a count.
- The card-timer issue in #1272 (timer counting from an earlier start). This change adds
  `startedAt` as the attempt's processing start but does not change the timer.
- Visual verification in a browser. I did not request a preview, so the card, status bar
  and drawer copy are covered by unit tests on the copy helper, not by a screenshot.
